At the outset learned counsel for the appellant submits that he does not want to press I.A.No.9877/2025, which is first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant-Narayan and insists for final hearing of this appeal.
There is no opposition to such prayer by the learned Government Advocate.
Accordingly, I.A.No.9877/2025 is dismissed as withdrawn.
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, appeal is heard finally.

2. This appeal is filed by the appellant/accused being aggrieved of the judgment dated 11.1.2025 passed by the learned Special Judge (POCSO Act), Khandwa in SC ATR No.99/2022 [State of M.P.
through P.S.Chhaigaonmakhan Vs. Narayan] whereby the appellant has been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50984 2 CRA-1743-2025 convicted under sections 376(2)(N), 376(3) of IPC &
sections 5(L) r/w 6 of the POCSO Act and section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and acquitted from charges u/s 363, 366 & 376 ('Gha') of IPC and he has been sentenced as under:-
In Fine default Sentence Imprisonment Amount of fine amount Rs.2,000/-

In short, prosecution story is that on 02.6.2022 in morning at about 11.00 am mother of the prosecutrix had gone for working as a labourer and when she returned from work, prosecutrix was not found at home.
She made search for prosecutrix and accordingly First Information Report (Ex.P/11) Crime No.257/2022 was registered under section 363 IPC and Missing Person Report (Exhibit-P/10) was lodged.
The case was investigated, in which, proof of age from the school record was obtained.
When prosecutrix was recovered she was medically examined.
Her statements were recorded.
After completing the other formalities charge-sheet was filed.
Accused denied the charges.
After evidence of prosecution witnesses, when accused was confronted with the prosecution evidence he again stated that he is innocent but did not lead any defence evidence in the trial Court.
4. This appeal has been filed on the ground that there are serious contradictions and omissions in the prosecution case.
It is not proved that on the date of incident the prosecutrix was less than 18 years of age.
Therefore, prayer has been made to allow the instant appeal and acquit the appellant.

5. On the other hand, learned Government Advocate supported the judgment NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50984 3 CRA-1743-2025 of the trial Court and submitted that it is well founded and same does not call for any interference by this Court on any ground.
6. We have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.

7. PW.1 (Kaluram) Headmaster of the School has stated that as per School Register (Exhibit-P/4)
the date of birth of prosecutrix is recorded as 19.8.2007.
In paragraph 4 of the cross-examination he stated that at the time of admission in school the date of birth certificate was not produced.

On his own he stated that date of birth is provided by 'Aganwadi' but in Exhibit-P/4 (Scholar Register)
there is no note or document to this effect that any information regarding date of birth was received from 'Aganwadi'.
In paragraph 6 he further stated that on Exhibit- P/5 (Progress Report) the first date of birth, which was mentioned, was informed on estimation.
8. PW.2 (prosecutrix) stated that she is 15 years of age and the incident is of six months ago.
In paragraph 5 of her cross-examination she stated that her date of birth is not recorded with her father and mother.
She also admitted that no proper birth certificate is issued by the Government to any member of the family.
In paragraph 6 she stated that her current age is 22 years.
The statement of the prosecutrix was recorded on 17.11.2022 and offence is of 02.6.2022.
In cross- examination she stated that before the incident she was married and had lived in a matrimonial home for about 08 months and then she came back.
She got married, when she was 18 years of age.
9. PW.3 (mother of the Prosecutrix) has stated in her examination-in-chief that prosecutrix is 15 years of age.
In paragraph 5 of her cross-examination she stated that she does not remember the date of birth of prosecutrix.

In paragraph 10 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50984 4 CRA-1743-2025 of her cross-examination she admitted that when she went to school to get children admitted then she had asked the Teacher to record the date of birth on his own estimation, looking to the height and health of children.
In paragraph 11 she stated that in School, Court and to the Police she has narrated the age of the prosecutrix by estimation.

sentences.text: PW.15 (father of the prosecutrix) in examination-in-chief has stated that on the date of incident the prosecutrix was of 15 years.

11. In view of above, when we appreciate the oral and documentary evidence on record we find that the prosecution has failed to prove that on the date of offence prosecutrix was less than 18 years,
especially in the light of statements of the prosecutrix (PW.2) made in paragraph 6 and that of her mother (PW.3) in paragraphs 5, 10 & 11.
Therefore, the finding of the learned trial Court regarding age of the prosecutrix in paragraph 34 is set aside.
Accordingly, it is held that on the date of offence prosecutrix is not proved to be minor, being less than 18 years.
12. Prosecutrix (PW.2) in paragraph 1 has stated that inspite of her objecting that she would go with the accused he took her on motorcycle to the house of Rohan and then he raped her many times.
She further stated that when appellant/Narayan went out of the room, thereafter Rohan came and he also raped her thrice.
Both of them raped her multiple times.
In paragraph 10 of her cross- examination she stated that on the date of incident appellant/Narayan did not do any wrong with her.
Thereafter, she went to her sister's house so as to her mother think as if she had gone to her sister's (Aarti) house.
In Aarti's house she had changed her clothes and had washed herself.
In paragraph 11 she stated that her mother assaulted her and lodged report against appellant/accused.
In paragraph 12 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50984 5 CRA-1743-2025 she stated that in school her date of birth was recorded on estimation looking to her height and health.
In paragraph 12 she stated that out of pressure of her mother she state to the Police and before Court regarding rape.
Appellant- Narayan has not done any wrong with her.
Thereafter, on re-examination by the prosecution as to whether appellant has raped her or not she has given contradictory statements in examination-in-chief and in cross-examination.
She stated that whatever she has stated in examination-in-chief is correct, and whatever she deposed in cross-examination is wrong.
It is worthwhile to note here that entire statements of the prosecutrix including examination-in-chief, cross-examination and re-examination was recorded on the same date.
In re- examination by the defence in paragraph 13, this witness again stated that she is stating about rape out of pressure of her mother, who is sitting in Court.
13. PW.7 (Dr.Ruplata Patel) has stated that on medical examination of the prosecutrix she did not found any injury on her body.
Her hymen was torn.

14. Therefore, looking to the medical evidence, as deposed by the Lady Doctor, and looking to the evidence of Prosecutrix (PW.2), who changed her version on the same date at a short intervals, as to whether appellant/accused did wrong with the prosecutrix and if any relationship was made whether the same was made against her will or with her consent, we find that her statements were changing frequently and the same cannot be relied upon, therefore, it cannot be said that the relationship which was made by her and is supported by DNA report (Ex.P/27), was against her consent.
15. Accordingly, appeal is allowed.
Impugned judgment of conviction and sentence by the trial Court is set aside.

Appellant is acquitted of the charges under section 376(2)(N), 376(3) of IPC & sections 5(L) r/w 6 of the POCSO Act NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50984 6 CRA-1743-2025 Narayan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192508971/
3 and section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

16. The disposal of the property shall be as per judgment of the trial Court.
